albums.blurb: Laraaji, born Edward Larry Gordon, was busking with an open-tuned zither in Washington Square Park when Brian Eno left a note in his instrument case inviting him to record. The result became the third installment of Eno's Ambient series, between Harold Budd's The Plateaux of Mirror and Eno's own On Land, and the only entry performed by an outside artist, with Eno producing and adding treatments. Three hypnotic hammered-dulcimer pieces titled "The Dance" fill the first side, and two slow zither "Meditation" pieces close the record; there are no voices anywhere on it.
albums.reception: AllMusic's review calls it "an early new age masterpiece" with "far more rigor, inventiveness, and sheer joy of playing than the great majority of its supposed descendents."

albums.blurb: Hill's only solo studio album, made when the Fugees went on hiatus and written and produced almost entirely by Hill herself, partly at Bob Marley's Tuff Gong studio in Kingston. Its title nods to Carter G. Woodson's 1933 book The Mis-Education of the Negro, and it folds hip-hop, reggae, and doo-wop into its soul framework, with guest turns from D'Angelo, Mary J. Blige, and Carlos Santana. It sits at the center of the late-90s neo soul moment alongside Erykah Badu's and D'Angelo's early records.
albums.reception: It debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with about 423,000 first-week copies, then a record for a female artist, and won five Grammys in 1999 including Album of the Year — the first hip-hop album to take that prize.

albums.blurb: A London songwriter, producer, and multi-instrumentalist, and the daughter of session bass great Pino Palladino. Jai Paul recruited her to his Paul Institute label in 2017, where she released a slow trickle of singles before this self-titled debut arrived on the XL imprint in April 2024. It is a meticulous piece of 80s-indebted studio R&B and synth-pop, co-produced with Jai Paul, who duets with her on "I Care."
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 88 out of 100 ("universal acclaim") and placed at No. 20 on Rough Trade's Albums of the Year 2024 list.
